R3B-bear-walk-0001.name: 2.5 km NE of Otter Creek
R3B-bear-walk-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R3B-bear-walk-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2014 (12 years old), 70 m E: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2021 (fire K21937), 400 m S: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 110 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Blue River, about 59 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Cedar St, Hwy 5, Otter Creek FSR, Otter Main FSR.
Park: 51.69959, -119.29049, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 1.6 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 446 m, about 77 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 3-41, Region 3. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R3B-bear-walk-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 3-41: about 128 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.14 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Beginner friendly
tags.why: Quieter spot only 1.6 km from the parking: fewer hunters, short walk back (Tip, estimate).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

R3B-grouse-walk-0003.name: 3.1 km NE of Otter Creek
R3B-grouse-walk-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
2 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
2 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

flags.t: Spot is inside a Motor Vehicle Closed Area: Thompson, Cariboo and Okanagan Alpines. Closed Year Round. Exemption: Snowmobiles exempt year round (January 1 to December 31). Synopsis map 1-82/24.
Above 1,700 m: in Region 3 no motor vehicles except snowmobiles, except on existing roads and trails (synopsis page 33, 99%). Elevation from terrain tiles (estimate).

seasonRows.notes: youth only: hunters under 18 (page footnote); New, printed green
MU 3-41 is not listed in the Region 3 sharp tailed grouse rows (my reading of the table).

plan: Drive: from Blue River, about 56 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.72183, -119.30445, pull off on V1815.00 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk 2.0 km to the start. Walk: the V1881.00 stretch, 5.7 km one way. About 115 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 3-41, Region 3. Season: grouse Sept 10 to Nov 30 and more rows (synopsis page 34, 99%). 3 legal flags below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R3B-grouse-walk-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 3-41: about 1,632 hunter days a year for all big game (2020 to 2024 mean), 1.75 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
